tasks.short: Recommend whether parties should accept or reject compromise settlement offers.

steps.what: Retrieve compromise offers and the relevant dispute evidence
Evaluate compromise settlement terms and choose an acceptance or rejection recommendation
Explain the compromise recommendation and discuss its implications with disputants
Record the recommendation, reasons, and disputants' responses

tasks.design: Configure native case views and a recommendation-note template in {DOCS}. The mediator still evaluates the offer and discusses the recommendation; the template reduces repeated case headings and reference formatting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offer versions and supporting references can be scattered, and recommendation notes repeat case identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case folders and reusable note fields can reduce navigation and repeated formatting.
tasks.still_hard: Settlement value depends on priorities, uncertainty, and the parties' willingness to compromise.
tasks.human_edge: The mediator weighs human interests and explains tradeoffs without deciding for the parties.
tasks.altitude: Spend slightly less time finding versions and formatting the recommendation record.

reach.task: Review legal consequences of a compromise term
reach.learn: Which terms need specialist interpretation before a recommendation

evidence.claim: Native case views and note templates could reduce version navigation and repeated record formatting while leaving settlement judgement human.

assumptions: Offer lookup, substantive judgement, discussion, and recommendation writing are separately included.
The mediator identifies case, offer revision, evidence references, recommendation, reasons, and party response in s1 and s4; s4's twelve retained hours include all substantive note capture.
Native views touch retrieval only; templates touch repeated identifiers and layout. No machine consumes an assumed settlement score or recommends acceptance.
Missing offer versions require manual retrieval. No formal acceptance, agreement execution, automatic send, or self-gate on the note save is proposed.
unknowns: Whether offer versions are already well organised
How much note preparation repeats headings and references
research_questions: Do native case views and a note template reduce preparation and recording time without losing reasoning or party responses?

incremental.description: Maintain case views and recommendation-note fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 case-navigation scenario: B=100, R=16+40+25+12=93; gross 7%, less 2 upkeep gives central net 5%; conservative 0-2%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare settlement agreements accurately reflecting the parties' agreed terms.

steps.what: Clarify the settlement terms that disputants have agreed
Record agreed parties, obligations, payment terms, and unresolved settlement points
Draft the settlement agreement from the recorded terms

loop.purpose: Draft agreement wording from explicit agreed terms
loop.input: Term record and permitted template clauses
loop.output: Draft agreement with every obligation linked to the term record
loop.check: Mediator checks party identity, obligations, scope, deadlines, amounts, releases, and that wording adds no unagreed commitment
loop.stop: One revision; ambiguous or legally unsupported clauses return to manual drafting or specialist advice
loop.why_not_simpler: Template filling handles standard fields but varied settlement obligations require checked wording

steps.what: Check the complete settlement agreement against the agreed terms
Send the checked settlement agreement to the correct disputants for signature

tasks.design: Use a native {DOCS} settlement template and bounded clause drafting from a captured term record. The mediator checks every obligation and performs a separate final-version and recipient check before issuing the agreement through {EMAIL} or {ESIGN}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Varied agreed terms must be converted into coherent agreement wording without changing their meaning.
tasks.enabler_now: Legal drafting tools can propose wording from selected sources and controlled templates.
tasks.still_hard: A polished clause can introduce a release or obligation that the parties never agreed.
tasks.human_edge: The mediator recognises ambiguity and protects the distinction between negotiated consent and drafted language.
tasks.altitude: Reduce initial agreement wording while retaining term capture and legal checking.

reach.learn: Which obligations need specialist drafting rather than template adaptation

evidence.claim: Libra provides legal drafting and research; this supports drafting capability, not validated settlement agreements or a local saving.

assumptions: Clarification, term recording, drafting, full agreement checking, and issue for signature are separate phases.
The mediator produces party identifiers, obligations, amounts, due dates, scope, agreed release terms, unresolved points, and source references in s2; all capture time is in its 15% share.
Native template configuration comes first. Missing or disputed terms remain unresolved and require manual clarification; no assistant infers consent.
S5 is one selected issue channel, not duplicate email and signature sends. It retains final contact checking and binds the checked agreement version; no party signs automatically.
Internal draft saves have no self-approval gate or saving credit. The gate is for the real external issue of the exact agreement.
unknowns: Whether confidential case material may enter the chosen workspace
research_questions: Does assisted drafting reduce total agreement preparation after checking every obligation against the term record?

already_counted.description: Draft correction and complete agreement review

incremental.description: Maintain permitted templates and review unagreed-clause error patterns

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked agreement version, parties, obligations, amounts, deadlines, scope, release terms, and signatory contacts checked before issue; changes require renewed checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 agreement-drafting scenario: B=100, R=20+15+18+25+10=88; gross 12%, less 5 upkeep gives central net 7%; conservative 0-3%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess valid claims and issue payment authorisations within delegated authority.

steps.what: Retrieve the claim, settlement basis, and delegated payment authority
Determine claim validity and authorise payment within delegated limits
Write the payment authorisation notice and its supporting reasons
Check and send the payment authorisation notice to the designated claims handler
Record the authorisation dispatch and any unresolved payment conditions

tasks.design: Configure a native claim evidence view and payment-authorisation notice template in {DOCS}. The arbitrator retains the validity and delegated-authority decision, checks the completed notice before its separate {EMAIL} send, and records dispatch afterward.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence lookup and repeated notice fields add work around the actual authorisation judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case views and templates can reuse controlled references without deciding validity or moving money.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed entitlement and limits of delegated authority require professional interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The arbitrator recognises when a claim lacks a defensible basis or exceeds the available authority.
tasks.altitude: Reduce lookup and notice formatting around retained claim authorisation.

reach.learn: Which claim conditions need further legal interpretation

evidence.claim: Native claim views and notice templates could reduce retrieval and repeated field formatting without deciding entitlement or executing payment.

assumptions: Lookup, the actual claim-authorisation decision, notice writing, sending, and post-send record entry are separate steps.

The claimant produces the claim and supporting evidence during the existing claim process. The arbitrator verifies claim identifier, claimant identity, amount, basis, conditions, and delegation version in s1 and s2; all verification time is retained.

The arbitrator enters authorisation scope, conditions, reasons, and evidence references in s3's sixteen retained hours. Native views touch retrieval and the template touches repeated labels and references only.

Missing evidence or uncertain delegation requires manual investigation and prevents authorisation. S2's gate is the task's substantive authorisation of another party's claim, not approval of the arbitrator's own notice save.

The designated claims handler is outside the arbitrator's organisation in this scenario. S4's gate covers the actual external notice and recipient; no bank payment, enterprise posting, or hidden send is proposed. S5 retains its full record-entry time.
unknowns: What payment authority the role actually holds
Whether claims-handler communication is internal or external in the organisation
Whether notice fields are already templated
research_questions: Can native claim views and a notice template reduce preparation time while preserving delegation and condition checks?

already_counted.description: Substantive claim validity and delegated-authority decision
Substantive notice writing and final recipient check

incremental.description: Maintain case views and authorisation notice fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact claim identifier, claim evidence version, claimant, authorised amount, conditions, and delegation version assessed in s2; changed claims require a new authorisation
Exact payment-authorisation notice, claim decision reference, conditions, and designated handler contact checked before sending; changes require renewed checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 retrieval-and-notice scenario: B=100, R=16+45+16+10+5=92; gross 8%, less 2 upkeep gives central net 6%; conservative 0-3%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interview claimants, agents, and witnesses and record their disputed-issue information.

steps.what: Review disputed issues and relevant case material before the interview
Interview claimants, agents, or witnesses about disputed issues
Capture interview notes with attribution, uncertainty, and source references
Write the interview summary from the attributed notes

loop.purpose: Organise attributed notes into a case interview summary
loop.input: Mediator's notes with speaker attribution and uncertainty
loop.output: Draft summary distinguishing assertions, observations, and unresolved points
loop.check: Mediator compares every summary statement to the notes and checks attribution, uncertainty, omissions, and absence of invented quotations
loop.stop: One revision; ambiguous statements remain unresolved or are summarised manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A native note template provides sections but cannot faithfully condense varied free text accounts

steps.what: Check the interview summary against notes and preserve unresolved contradictions

tasks.design: Keep the interview and attributed note capture with the mediator in {DOCS}. Test native note sections first, then use bounded drafting for the summary while retaining a separate completeness and attribution check.
tasks.previous_blocker: The interview account must be condensed into a usable record without changing what was actually said.
tasks.enabler_now: Source restricted summarisation can organise supplied notes while preserving unresolved fields for human checking.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, hesitation, contradictions, and questions requiring follow-up remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: The mediator listens carefully and distinguishes a party's assertion from an established fact.
tasks.altitude: Reduce summary prose work while retaining listening, note capture, and credibility judgement.

reach.task: Review interview attribution and evidential limits
reach.learn: Which paraphrases could misrepresent a witness account

evidence.claim: A bounded assistant could condense attributed interview notes, with human checking required for attribution and evidential meaning.

assumptions: The written interview record is included. Conversation time in s2 excludes note-writing time allocated separately to s3, even when those activities alternate during the same interview.
The mediator produces speaker identifier, interview date, question or topic, attributed statement, uncertainty, contradiction, and note locator in s3; its 15% share includes all note capture.
Native note headings touch record structure but receive no saving credit for substantive capture. Drafting touches summary prose in s4 only; its six retained hours include correction.
No recording, automatic transcription, credibility score, inferred fact, or invented quotation is proposed. Incomplete notes require manual summary or follow-up, not reconstruction by a model.
Confidentiality and permitted workspace use must be confirmed. No summary send or self-approval gate on the internal save is implied.
unknowns: Whether case confidentiality permits assisted summarisation
How much current recording is notes versus full transcription
research_questions: Does summary drafting reduce total record time while preserving every material attribution and unresolved contradiction?

already_counted.description: Summary correction and final attribution check

incremental.description: Maintain summary guidance and review attribution errors

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 interview-summary scenario: B=100, R=10+60+15+6+5=96; gross 4%, less 2 upkeep gives central net 2%; conservative 0-1%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep dispute judgement and personal dialogue while making written case outcomes easier to prepare and trace.
reach: Refer unusual clauses and entitlement issues to lawyers
Compare witness-note attribution with legal colleagues
role.ambitious_version: A mediator or arbitrator with clearer case records and less repeated drafting, retaining consent, credibility, and legal judgement.
